description: Neural Amp Modeler player: it runs a captured amp model over a mono guitar signal, with a noise gate in front of the model and a five-band equaliser after it

params.text: Sets the gain into the amp model, silent fully anticlockwise and twice the input voltage fully clockwise
Sets the gain out of the amp model, from silence to double, after which the signal is limited to 7.5V either way
Sets the level below which the noise gate closes, -80dB to 0dB
Sets how quickly the gate opens once the signal rises past the threshold, 0.1ms to 50ms
Sets how quickly the gate closes once the hold time has run out, 10ms to 500ms
Sets how long the gate stays open after the signal drops below the threshold, 10ms to 500ms
A low shelf at 100Hz on the model's output, 12dB of cut fully anticlockwise and 12dB of boost fully clockwise, flat in the middle
A peaking filter at 650Hz on the model's output, 12dB of cut fully anticlockwise and 12dB of boost fully clockwise, flat in the middle
A high shelf at 3200Hz on the model's output, 12dB of cut fully anticlockwise and 12dB of boost fully clockwise, flat in the middle
A peaking filter at 3500Hz on the model's output, 12dB of cut fully anticlockwise and 12dB of boost fully clockwise, flat in the middle
A peaking filter at 80Hz on the model's output, 12dB of cut fully anticlockwise and 12dB of boost fully clockwise, flat in the middle

inputs.text: The guitar or line signal to be amplified, mono, with 5V taken as the model's full scale
Takes over the input gain while patched, -5V for silence and 5V for double gain; the knob does nothing while a cable is in here
Takes over the output gain while patched, -5V for silence and 5V for double gain; the knob does nothing while a cable is in here
Takes over the gate threshold while patched, -5V for -80dB and 5V for 0dB; the knob does nothing while a cable is in here
Takes over the gate attack while patched, -5V for 0.1ms and 5V for 50ms; the knob does nothing while a cable is in here
Takes over the gate release while patched, -5V for 10ms and 5V for 500ms; the knob does nothing while a cable is in here
Takes over the gate hold while patched, -5V for 10ms and 5V for 500ms; the knob does nothing while a cable is in here
Takes over the BASS control while patched, -5V for a 12dB cut and 5V for a 12dB boost; the knob does nothing while a cable is in here
Takes over the MID control while patched, -5V for a 12dB cut and 5V for a 12dB boost; the knob does nothing while a cable is in here
Takes over the TRBL control while patched, -5V for a 12dB cut and 5V for a 12dB boost; the knob does nothing while a cable is in here
Takes over the PRES control while patched, -5V for a 12dB cut and 5V for a 12dB boost; the knob does nothing while a cable is in here
Takes over the DPTH control while patched, -5V for a 12dB cut and 5V for a 12dB boost; the knob does nothing while a cable is in here

outputs.text: The amp model's output, mono, limited to 7.5V either way

notes: the module passes its input through with the two level knobs applied and nothing else until a model is loaded from the right-click menu
every CV input here replaces its knob rather than adding to it: while a cable is patched, -5V to 5V covers the whole range of that control and the knob is out of circuit
the display across the top is a bar meter of the output signal, and it prints ECO ON in the corner while Eco Mode is on
the green lamp lights when a model is loaded and glows at half brightness while one is loading
the yellow lamp lights when the loaded model was captured at a different sample rate from the engine, which is resampled to match
the red lamp lights while the noise gate is closed
the NAM FX Loop expander goes immediately to the right of this module and inserts its send and return between the amp model and this module's output jack
menu: Bundled Models — lists the model files that ship with the plugin; picking one loads it
Load Custom Model... — opens a file dialogue for a .nam model file anywhere on disk
Unload Model — drops the loaded model, leaving the module passing its input through
Eco Mode: Off, On — averages each pair of samples and runs the model once per pair, for about half the processor cost
Use Fast Tanh — computes the model's activation function from an approximation rather than the library function, for less processor cost
Waveform Color: Green, Baby Blue, Amber, Red, Purple, White — sets the colour of the bars in the output display
